claims: The Artemis II crew safely returned to Earth on Friday, April 10, 2026.
The Artemis II crew splashed down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego at 8:07 p.m. EDT (5:07 p.m. PDT).
The four astronauts concluded a 10-day mission.
The mission marked the first human trip to the Moon and back in over 50 years.
The Orion capsule touched down in the Pacific Ocean.
Recovery teams were stationed to retrieve the crew.
The astronauts were reported as "happy and healthy" following the high-speed re-entry.
The crew was transported to the USS John P. Murtha for initial medical evaluations.
The crew returned to NASA's Johnson Space Center in Houston.
The mission successfully tested the systems needed to send future astronauts back to the Moon and eventually to Mars.
